messages.subject: Model averaging variations of the same model
parts:
I am performing an occu() model in two steps due to having a large number of covariates. I am also interested in looking at quadratic and logarithmic relationships. In the end for some of my species models there is no significant difference between all the fetch models. 

                            Models          K   AICc dAICc weight
14         psi(c + fetch + easting)   4 146.17  0.00   0.19
2           psi(c + fetch^2)              3 146.74  0.57   0.14
             psi(c + fetch)                 3 146.81  0.64   0.14
12         psi(c + distLake)            3 147.55  1.38   0.10
10         psi(c + easting)              3 147.58  1.41   0.09
4           psi(c + logfetch)             3 147.60  1.43   0.09

My first question is:
Do I need to average all of these models, this may be a somewhat frustrating process or can I make the argument that I looked at fetch^2, log(fetch), and fetch and decided that the fetch^2 relationship was the strongest "fetch relationship", and just keep that for the remainder of my analysis.

My second question is:
When performing my detection modeling process, should I just use the top model rather than an averaged model? Or should I use a general model from the top models (i.e. fetch^2 + easting + distLake)

Thanks,
Eric
